clue.text: Mentioning cut in content of fruitcake?

indicators.note: cut here means the word is docked, losing its final letter

parts.note: raising a subject means mentioning it, so the participle matches

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether bringing up a cut is part of what goes into a fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final G from RAISING. 'Cut' looks like the thing being mentioned, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are a staple ingredient baked into fruitcake, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Endure a lesser song that has not succeeded

indicators.note: a song that has not got the letter for succeeded means that letter is removed

parts.note: the B-side of a single is its less important track
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A minor track that flopped is something to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that has not' removes S (succeeded) from B-SIDE, the less important track on the back of a single record.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate or bear it, a straightforward synonym of endure.

clue.text: Extremely limiting volume in gabbling etc, in this way primarily?

definitions.text: Extremely limiting volume in gabbling etc, in this way primarily?

indicators.note: primarily says this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: so means in this way, as in 'do it so'

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces inside the shuffled letters
gabbling suggests garbled speech, so the letters of etc are jumbled
limiting means the word too encloses the letter for volume, bounding it

parts.note: too means extremely, as in 'too kind'

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping your voice right down while gabbling on about et cetera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' and 'in' are both containment signals, nested one inside the other; 'gabbling' scrambles 'etc' and 'primarily' sets the start. Read whole, the clue describes speaking under one's breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking sotto voce means in an undertone, drastically reducing the loudness of one's speech.

clue.text: Potent drink? Note people getting uppity after swallowing half of it

indicators.note: swallowing means the reversed people take in the other piece
in a down clue going up means the letters read backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is one letter, here its second

explanation.surface: A strong drink making a crowd of people get above themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting uppity' turns RACE to ECAR, and 'swallowing' puts T (half of 'it') inside: ECTAR after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, giving immortality, so a potent drink indeed.

clue.text: Cybernetics book in support, backing science

indicators.note: in places the letter for book inside the word for support

parts.note: to root for someone is to support them

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation is written backwards

explanation.surface: A cybernetics textbook getting behind the science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is the verb sense, as in rooting for a team; 'in' and 'backing' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Cybernetics, the study of control systems in machines, is closely allied to the engineering of automated machines.

clue.text: Resort hosting new student and something for the old hand

indicators.note: hosting means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a recourse is something you resort to, so one resort
a fresher is a first-year university student

explanation.surface: A holiday resort entertaining a first-year student and a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' is the containment signal. 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but means a fallback; 'fresher' is British slang for a first-year undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced workers take refresher training to update skills they learned long ago.

clue.text: Many Americans are keen on this immoral dance

definitions.text: Many Americans are keen on this

parts.note: base means low and immoral
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Plenty of Americans enjoy a wicked dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the national pastime of the USA, followed by millions of fans.

clue.text: Cheers with adoption of current measure in US city

indicators.note: adoption means the thanks takes the unit inside it

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks
amp, short for ampere, measures electric current

explanation.surface: A toast as an American city adopts a new electrical standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with adoption of' signals containment; 'Cheers' is the British informal thank-you, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Charlie and Mike probed by a detective chap's line of questioning

indicators.note: probed means the outer letters have the other pieces pushed into them

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet
M is Mike in the NATO alphabet
tec is short for detective
his means belonging to a chap

explanation.surface: Two men grilled by a detective in an interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probed by' means the two NATO-alphabet letters are split apart by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a set of questions and answers, so the term fits any series of probing questions.

clue.text: Fighting? Son in outburst is receiving restraint

indicators.note: in places the letter for son inside the outburst

parts.note: a fit is a sudden outburst, of temper say

indicators.note: receiving means is takes the restraint inside it

parts.note: a cuff, as in handcuff, restrains

explanation.surface: A son having a tantrum ends up in handcuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containments side by side, signalled by 'in' and 'receiving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fisticuffs is an old-fashioned word for a fight with bare fists.

clue.text: Energy corporation backed without comment?

indicators.note: backed means the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
corporation is jocular slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: An energy company supported but making no statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' here is old jokey slang for a large belly (TUM); 'backed' reverses E + TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays silent offers no remark, as though they cannot speak.

clue.text: French newspaper used to absorb a drink

indicators.note: absorbing means the newspaper takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily

explanation.surface: A Parisian paper is used to mop up a spilt drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to absorb' puts A inside LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink made with lemons, water and sugar.

clue.text: Part of chain? Refuse 40% of chain

parts.note: bran is the husks left as refuse when grain is milled

indicators.note: forty per cent of a five-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A link in a chain rejects a chunk of the chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, the chaff left over: BRAN. '40% of' takes the first two of the five letters of 'chain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of shops is made up of individual outlets, each one a local office of the group.

clue.text: Too small to block a great deal? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped
blocking means the letter sits inside the phrase, obstructing it

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Is something too small to obstruct much? Only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to block' puts S inside A LOT to give ALSOT, and 'Not entirely' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: Keeps articles in records: nothing identifying dog

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces within the records

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
has means keeps or holds
a and a are two indefinite articles
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone keeps cuttings about records, with nothing to identify a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment; 'articles' gives two copies of the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired Tibetan breed of dog.

clue.text: Jerk, lacking completeness, adopting inclination regarding completeness

indicators.note: adopting means the shortened word takes the lean inside it
lacking completeness means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to hoick is British slang for to jerk or yank something upwards
a list is a ship's lean or inclination

explanation.surface: A jerk who is incomplete taking on a leaning about wholeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking completeness' docks the last letter of a British slang word for yank; 'adopting' then signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A holistic approach treats the whole of something rather than its separate parts.

clue.text: Get moving as a way of creating gale?

parts.note: read as wordplay, shake signals an anagram of the letters A and LEG, which produces gale

explanation.surface: A question about a way of whipping up a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction says rearrange A LEG, which gives GALE: a reverse clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake a leg is an idiom urging someone to hurry up and get going.

clue.text: It is found in Eastern sea with a list

indicators.note: found in means is sits inside the sea letters

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Something is located in an eastern sea along with an inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals containment; the Med is the usual crossword sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Itemised describes something set out item by item, as an inventory would be.

clue.text: Old woman getting more elegant — she's had lots of admirers

parts.note: ma is mother, the old woman
neater means tidier or more elegant

explanation.surface: An elderly lady growing smarter, with a string of suitors behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for mother here, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a woman who attracts and discards many lovers.

clue.text: Bats heading off in horde

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, as is barmy

explanation.surface: Bats fly off at the front of a swarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' is the adjective, crazy (BARMY), not the animals; 'heading off' drops B.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a vast crowd or multitude, like a horde.

clue.text: Record of history is silent about exploit

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: keeping mum means staying silent
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: History's record keeps quiet about some heroic deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploit' looks like a noun (a feat), but it is the verb USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum preserves objects as a record of the past.

clue.text: Border flower put at the front will lead to chaos

indicators.note: put at the front means the flower goes before the border

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Planting a flower at the front of a border will cause havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border flower' reads as one garden phrase but splits in two; 'put at the front' reorders them. May is hawthorn blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or confusion.

clue.text: Pigeon in roost at the outset

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: at the outset means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A pigeon settled on its perch from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the synonym HOME, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, bred to fly back to its loft.

clue.text: Old British currency's restricted limits to usual wealth

indicators.note: restricted means the coins hem in the other letters

parts.note: pence are British coins

indicators.note: limits are the boundary letters of the word

explanation.surface: Former British money kept within the bounds of normal riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old British currency' wants to be one phrase, but Old stands alone. 'limits to' picks the outer letters and 'restricted' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great luxury and riches.

clue.text: Dancer's colleague to turn up on time

parts.note: to come is to arrive, to turn up

explanation.surface: A dancer's partner arriving punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer and Comet are two of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Comet pulls Santa's sleigh in the same team as the reindeer Dancer.

clue.text: Plans to return to get unwanted mail

indicators.note: returning means reading the word backwards

parts.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Schemes come back as junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email sent in bulk to people who did not ask for it.

clue.text: Current and power securing sources of every town's light — such as this?

definitions.text: Current and power securing sources of every town's light — such as this?

indicators.note: securing means the current and power hold the other letters inside

parts.note: a stream is a current of water

indicators.note: sources are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Electricity and power reach every town's lights, as in a public lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity but is a flow of water. 'sources of' picks initials and 'securing' signals containment; read whole, the clue describes a street light.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetlamp is a public light powered by electric current, found in every town.

clue.text: Breakfast food in kitchen store unopened after finishing off meat

indicators.note: after says the store's letters follow the meat's in the answer
finishing off means the last letter is lost

parts.note: pork is a meat

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a fridge stores food in a kitchen

explanation.surface: Breakfast found in an unopened fridge after the meat has been eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops a first letter and 'finishing off' a last one; 'after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is oats boiled in milk or water, a classic breakfast dish.

clue.text: Strong male, important after our team slips

indicators.note: slips means those letters slip out of the word

parts.note: weighty means important
we is how a team refers to itself

explanation.surface: A tough man becomes significant once his side loses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' removes WE ('our team') from WEIGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means powerful or very strong.
